content:
Earlier this year, Apple closed part of the Apple Park Visitor Center to carry out "store improvement works."

The area has now reopened, with the biggest change being that Apple has removed the augmented reality (AR) experience that allowed visitors to view Apple Park through specially made iPads.

When Apple opened the Apple Park Visitor Center to the public in 2017, it introduced the AR experience in the following way:

Using augmented reality to bring a three-dimensional model of the campus to life, inviting visitors to explore Apple Park in an immersive, interactive way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building and see one of the largest on-site solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof to peek at the layout of the collaborative office spaces inside.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three sections: the AR exhibit, a traditional Apple Store, and a café.

Apple has now retired the AR exhibit and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. As discovered by MacRumors, the walls feature Avenues display shelves showcasing accessories, along with redesigned product display tables holding a range of Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the café, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but after nine years, the space seems to have found a more fitting new purpose.

I had originally hoped Apple would not simply convert it into a standard retail store, but try something else. Luckily, at least the café has been kept as a distinctive feature of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
